subject: Phased data disposal and field-level redaction options for PHI
messages:
From: Sarah Levine <slevine@medsys.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data lifecycle question: retention limits and redaction for PHI

Hi Alex,

We're evaluating Redwood for a controlled rollout that will process patient intake forms and follow-up notes. Our security team needs a clear answer on two fronts before we proceed: 1) retention limits for PHI-bearing artifacts (both in the hosted API and under a Dedicated/Private deployment), including backups and logs, and 2) redaction/pseudonymization options we can apply at ingestion or at rest so that certain fields (SSNs, MRNs, free-text clinical notes) are not stored as identifiable data.

Some specific asks:
- Can we configure a per-field retention window (for example, keep analytics-safe pseudonymized IDs for 7 years but purge raw PHI after 30 days)?
- What does permanent deletion look like (soft-delete vs cryptographic erase)? How do you handle backups and audit trails?
- Are there reversible tokenization options for analytics (so we can re-link records for legal holds) and how are keys managed?

We expect to be asked about eDiscovery and audit exports by legal; any recommended artifacts we should plan to request?

Thanks,
Sarah
Dr. Sarah Levine
Head of Compliance
MedSys Health

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Levine <slevine@medsys.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle question: retention limits and redaction for PHI

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, followed by a suggested next step and an attachment with a checklist.

High level:
- Per-field retention: Yes — across Dedicated and Private deployments you can apply field-level retention policies. Hosted API supports data retention windows by dataset and route; field-level redaction is supported via ingestion transforms.
- Deletion semantics: We support soft-delete with 30-day grace by default; permanent purge can be coordinated (cryptographic key zeroization available in Private with HSM/KMS). Backups are subject to the same retention policy when running under Dedicated/Private; hosted backups follow our standard retention (we'll provide the export).
- Reversible tokenization: Redwood supports deterministic tokenization (format-preserving or token vault with reversible mapping) as an option under Dedicated/Private. Keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM for Private deployments to meet legal-hold/relinking requirements.

What we'll provide in the doc/attachment:
- A decision matrix (attached) that maps each PHI class to recommended handling (immediate redaction, pseudonymize, keep raw for X days)
- Steps for configuring ingestion transforms and the deletion API you can call for expedited purge
- A list of artifacts for eDiscovery (audit logs, model request bodies, deletion receipts) and how to export them

Next step: Dylan (cc'd) will follow up with the technical implementation options (regex vs model-assisted redaction, KV cache handling, backup retention). Can we schedule a 30-min deep-dive tomorrow?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-data-disposal-checklist.pdf

Thanks Alex — that sounds promising. A couple clarifying points from Legal/Engineering:

- Backups: if we request an immediate permanent purge, what guarantees do we have that an older backup can't be used to recover PHI? Is there a documented process to confirm backup purge or key destruction?
- KV cache and model context: will cached token-level context be included in the deletion/purge? Is there a window where short-term KV is inevitable and how long does it persist?
- Analytics: we need to run cohort analytics for quality of care on de-identified data for up to 7 years. Ideally we'd pseudonymize MRNs with reversible mapping under our control.

Please have Dylan include specifics and the API/operational steps we can hand to our security ops team.

Sarah

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data lifecycle question: retention limits and redaction for PHI

Hi Sarah — following up with the technical specifics you can hand to Security Ops. Long version below; happy to hop on the deep-dive.

1) Backups and permanent purge
- Hosted: backups are managed by Redwood and follow our backup retention schedule. For hosted customers we provide deletion receipts and exports; full cryptographic key zeroization is only available for Private with customer-managed keys. We can produce a documented purge certificate for hosted deletions and coordinate with Legal for eDiscovery timelines.
- Dedicated/Private: you can opt into key rotation/zeroization. When keys tied to encrypted backups are zeroized, the data effectively becomes unrecoverable. We include a backup purge verification checklist and can provide the post-purge SHA summaries. See attached checklist.

2) KV cache, model context, and ephemeral storage
- KV cache in the serving runtime is considered ephemeral and is cleared on soft-delete windows. However, in high-throughput scenarios short-lived cache shards might persist for a small window (minutes to hours) depending on batching. For regulated workflows we recommend: 1) disabling persistent KV cache for inputs containing raw PHI, or 2) applying ingestion redaction to strip PHI before it ever hits the cache.

3) Field-level redaction and pseudonymization options
- Ingestion transforms (pre-store): regex-based redaction, model-assisted redaction (PII/PHI taggers), and deterministic tokenization using a token vault.
- At-rest transforms: field masking, reversible tokenization (token vault) with keys in your KMS, and format-preserving encryption (FPE) for analytics-friendly IDs.
- Tradeoffs: regex is simple but brittle for free text; model-assisted redaction is higher recall but requires prompt evaluation and a verification pass. Deterministic tokenization enables joins across datasets but requires secure key management and an access control model for re-identification.

4) Retention policy patterns we recommend
- Immediate redaction: SSNs, full MRNs, raw clinical notes containing direct identifiers — redact on ingest and only retain pseudonymized outputs for analytics.
- Staged retention: keep pseudonymized IDs + audit-safe metadata for 7 years; keep raw artifacts (where necessary) for up to 30 days behind a strict access control and approval workflow.
- Legal hold: we maintain immutable hold flags at the record level; a legal hold prevents automated purge until lifted. We also emit an export package (logs + record ids + deletion receipts) for eDiscovery.

5) Operational APIs and artifacts
- Deletion API: POST /v1/records/delete (supports record selectors and retention tags); returns a deletion_receipt_id
- Purge verification: GET /v1/records/delete/status?receipt_id=...
- Audit exports: /v1/audit/export (CSV/JSON) with signed timestamps for compliance

6) Implementation checklist (action items)
- Decide which fields are immediately redact vs pseudonymize
- Choose tokenization model (vault vs FPE) and decide who manages keys (Redwood KMS or customer KMS/HSM)
- Configure ingestion pipeline: apply model-assisted tagger + deterministic tokenization step
- Run small-scale evals on sample notes to validate recall/precision of redaction
- Schedule a 30-min runbook review with your Security Ops to walk deletion/purge flows

I'll attach the field-redaction-options-matrix.xlsx with suggested defaults. If helpful, we can draft an ERASURE/DELETION runbook and a short SOC2-ready artifact pack for your legal team.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Product Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
